name: Nubia RedMagic 12 Pro+
gaming_notes: Purpose-built esports flagship: Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 + Red Core R5 co-processor, 185Hz 1.5K OLED with 960Hz touch sampling, active liquid cooling, bypass charging for sustained peak performance, and shoulder-trigger-style game controls. The 8,400mAh battery outlasts most flagships. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: itel City 300 5G
gaming_notes: The Unisoc T8200 and a 120Hz screen handle casual titles and free-to-play games like Free Fire at modest settings, but the HD+ display, 10W charging and entry-level GPU mean it is not a pick for heavy gamers. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 Pro Refreshed Edition
gaming_notes: The Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 with a 120Hz adaptive OLED and a huge 9,000mAh battery make this a strong mid-range gaming pick with all-day sessions; IP69-rated build adds durability. 67W charging refills quickly. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Tecno Pova Curve 2 5G
gaming_notes: The Dimensity 7100 with Ice Cooling 3.0, a 144Hz curved AMOLED (2160Hz instant touch sampling) and bypass charging make this a strong mid-range gaming pick — TECNO claims 90 minutes of stable Free Fire at 60fps. The 8,000mAh battery stretches long sessions, though 45W charging needs ~82 minutes for a full refill. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Motorola Moto g37 5G
gaming_notes: The Dimensity 6300 runs PUBG Mobile smoothly on medium settings; the 120Hz LCD keeps casual games fluid. Don't expect high-refresh competitive gaming at this price. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: OnePlus 16
gaming_notes: Built for esports: Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 plus the Fengchi Gaming Kernel, dedicated G3 (network), T3 (touch) and P4 (display) gaming chips, a 185Hz gaming mode and one-click 'Gun God Mode', with a 9,000mAh battery, bypass charging and the Glacier Cooling System for long sessions.

name: HONOR 600S
gaming_notes: The Snapdragon 4 Gen 4 is an entry-level 5G chip for casual games and everyday use; demanding titles need low settings. The 120Hz display keeps the interface smooth.

name: Oppo F35 Pro 5G
gaming_notes: The Dimensity 7360 MAX with a large vapor chamber runs popular titles well at high settings; the 144Hz 1.5K AMOLED makes gameplay fluid, though it is a mid-range chip, not a flagship gaming SoC.

name: Sony Xperia 10 VIII
gaming_notes: The Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 handles everyday games at medium settings on the 120Hz OLED, but demanding 3D titles stutter and push the Adreno 710 to its limits.

name: Vivo Y600s Pro
gaming_notes: The Dimensity 7300e is a solid mid-range gaming chip that handles popular titles at high settings; the 120Hz AMOLED keeps motion smooth, though the huge battery is the real star for long sessions.
